title: When the Homecoming Sings
premise: Felix Lockridge, a trans girl who has spent five years passing as invisible at Hollow Creek High, is assigned a college essay prompt that asks students to name the truth they've never said aloud. Her answer leaks, and the school's beloved homecoming tradition — built on the buried history of a girl the town erased — becomes both her refuge and her trial. To survive the fallout, Felix must lead the underdog quiz team to a championship nobody cares about while fighting to sing the homecoming solo that would finally claim her voice in public. She wins neither cleanly: she loses the quiz final on purpose to expose the principal's cover-up of the school's history, and when the chosen soloist walks offstage, Felix sings anyway, uninvited, and the gymnasium remembers what it buried.
about_author: Mara Almeida is a former debate coach from coastal Maine who writes stories about kids who refuse to be footnotes. She lives with her partner, two loud cats, and a growing collection of unopened college brochures.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: POV Felix. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the senior essay prompt: 'Name the truth you have never said aloud.' Felix writes three safe drafts before 2 a.m., then one honest sentence she swears she'll delete. Emotional beat: the crack in the armor — longing disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Five Years of Careful
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Flashback-woven chapter establishing Felix's move to Hollow Creek at thirteen, her rules for invisibility, and her mother's loving but fragile silence about who Felix is. Beat: grief for the girl she postponed being.

chapters.title: Something Under the Gym
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Researching local history for extra credit, Felix finds a 1971 article about a student singer, Odile Marsh, whose name was struck from every trophy case after a scandal the article refuses to name. Beat: curiosity sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Ms. Okafor's anonymous peer-review swap misfires; Felix's honest draft lands in the wrong hands and screenshots spread by Monday. Beat: exposure — the exact catastrophe she engineered her life to avoid.

chapters.title: Hallway Weather
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The school splits: some cruelty, unexpected kindness, and total silence from her best friend Priya. Principal Dr. Voss calls it 'a distraction' and quietly cancels the essay assignment. Beat: loneliness with an audience.

chapters.title: Priya's Door
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya admits she froze out of fear, not betrayal, and shows Felix a box of her own secrets. Their friendship re-forms on new, honest terms. Beat: repair — belonging rebuilt deliberately rather than assumed.

chapters.title: Quiz Team Tryouts
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Needing a transcript line for scholarship applications, Felix joins the doomed quiz team run by burned-out coach Mr. Ansel. She's brilliant and hates being seen as brilliant. Beat: competence as camouflage beginning to fail.

chapters.title: Odile's Songbook
chapters.summary: POV Felix. In the archive basement, Felix finds Odile Marsh's handwritten songbook and a letter naming Voss's predecessor — and the district — as the ones who erased her. Beat: memory as inheritance; Felix decides someone should be remembered out loud.

chapters.title: The Solo Auditions
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Homecoming solo auditions are announced; the winner sings at the assembly. Felix, terrified, signs up anyway — then chokes mid-audition when Voss watches from the back. Beat: fear winning round one.

chapters.title: Ansel's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Mr. Ansel. The coach reveals he was Odile's classmate and has spent forty years not testifying. He agrees to help Felix dig, warning her the town protects its story. Beat: complicity across generations, and the choice to stop.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The ragtag quiz team overperforms; Felix carries them, and for one night the school cheers her without conditions. Beat: belonging tasted, which makes everything riskier.

chapters.title: What Voss Knows
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix requests a meeting and offers Voss a trade: restore Odile's name, and Felix stays quiet about the letter. Voss declines and threatens Felix's transcripts. Beat: the institution choosing itself.

chapters.title: The Essay That Wasn't Due
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix submits her real essay anyway, addressed to no admissions office — just filed publicly in the library's student anthology. Beat: reclaiming authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Someone reports the quiz team for an eligibility technicality traced to Voss's office. Priya finds the paper trail. Beat: injustice made concrete and documentable.

chapters.title: Small Mutinies
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Students begin leaving notes in Odile's old locker; the choir secretly rehearses her recovered song. Felix realizes she started something bigger than herself. Beat: hope as contagion.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix, Ansel, and Priya present the evidence to the school board; the board tables it 'pending review,' and Voss suspends Ansel. Beat: the system failing publicly — despair before defiance.

chapters.title: State Championship Eve
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Cleared to compete after public outcry, the team faces the final. Felix drafts a plan: if they win, she'll use the microphone. Priya makes her promise to win or lose honestly. Beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Final Question
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Tied match, last question — about local history, cruelly. Felix knows the answer includes Odile's erased name. She gives it fully, naming Odile on stage, forfeiting the protest ruling that would have won the title. Beat: sacrifice as testimony.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Loud
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The clip goes viral; alumni corroborate Ansel's account; the board reopens the case and suspends Voss pending investigation. Beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfectly, through collective pressure.

chapters.title: The Audition That Mattered
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Voss, before leaving, revokes the choir solo list entirely — no homecoming solo will be sung. The choir, led by students, votes to break the rule. Beat: the community choosing Felix back.

chapters.title: When the Homecoming Sings
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At the assembly, the announced program ends in silence — then Felix walks onstage uninvited and sings Odile's song, changing one verse to her own name. The gym stands. Beat: climax of voice — terror transfigured into presence.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Plaque
chapters.summary: POV Felix, months later. A restored plaque bears both names; Odile Marsh attends in person, elderly, and thanks Felix. Felix mails her college essay — the true one — and gets in. Beat: resolution — belonging earned, memory restored, future opened.
